name: Cold storage operators
shape_facts: Capacity and number of chambers, and whether chilled, frozen or controlled-atmosphere
Products stored: potatoes, fruit, vegetables, dates, meat, fish, dairy, frozen foods, pharma
Business model: rented space to farmers and traders, own trading stock, or 3PL for brands and importers
How rent is charged: per sack, per crate, per pallet, per month, per season
Power source and backup: grid, generator, solar
Number of clients and whether they collect stock in parts
Whether they also offer transport (reefer trucks)
scope_rule: pi notes business and operational problems: inward and outward records, client stock balances, rent billing and collection, space utilisation, power and diesel costs, breakdowns and downtime, claims from clients over damage, staff and gate control, and reporting. pi does not advise on refrigeration engineering, ammonia or refrigerant handling, storage temperatures for specific produce, food-safety or pharma storage rules, insurance claims or contract law. It does not store clients’ names, CNICs, trade licences or phone numbers; it records roles and counts.

vocabulary.chamber: insulated room within the cold store
vocabulary.gate pass / raseed: receipt issued when stock comes in, presented to take it out
vocabulary.rent per bori: storage charge per sack for the season
vocabulary.CA store: controlled-atmosphere store for long-term fruit storage
vocabulary.blast freezer: fast-freezing room for meat, fish or prepared food
vocabulary.3PL: third-party logistics, storing and dispatching for other companies
vocabulary.shrinkage / weight loss: loss of weight in stored produce over time (pi notes the dispute, not the science)

problems.phrase: Client says he stored 500 bags, our register shows 470
Stock taken out in parts and the balance per client gets confused
Bags end up in the wrong chamber and take hours to find
Some clients’ stock went missing and we had to pay
Gate passes are handwritten and can be copied
Rent collection at season end is a fight
Traders leave stock and disappear when prices fall
Diesel for generators during load shedding is killing margins
Electricity bill keeps rising and I don’t know per chamber cost
Compressor failed at night and nobody noticed till morning
Temperature logs are filled in at the end of the week, not actually checked
Client claims produce rotted in our store
Half empty in summer, full and turning people away in season
Rates differ client to client and no one remembers what was agreed
Night shift staff sleep or leave the gate open
Labourers for loading are hard to find in peak days
Trucks queue at the gate for hours
Brands we store for want daily stock reports, we send them by hand
3PL client orders come by email and WhatsApp and some get missed
Expiry dates on frozen stock not tracked per batch
Food authority inspection paperwork takes days
I’m away and can’t see if the store is running at the right temperature
Few new clients find us, it’s all word of mouth
Thinking of adding a chamber but don’t know if utilisation justifies it

records: How is stock recorded when it comes in and goes out?
client balances: When a client takes stock out in parts, how do you track what’s left?
How often do clients dispute it?
location: How do staff know where a client’s stock is in the store?
billing: How is rent charged and when?
What happens at season end with unpaid rent?
power: What’s your backup when the power goes?
How do you track diesel against generator hours?
breakdowns: How would you find out if a chamber’s temperature went wrong at night?
claims: Have clients claimed for damaged produce?
utilisation: How full are you in the off season compared to peak?
staff and gate: Who controls the gate at night?
3pl clients: Do any clients want regular stock reports?
How do you send them now?
growth: What would you need to see before adding capacity?

seasons: Pakistan potato stores fill after the main potato harvest (roughly January–March) and release through summer and autumn; fruit stores fill with kinnow (December–March), apples (August–October) and mango for short holds in summer; summer load shedding and heat raise diesel and power costs sharply (May–September). Eid ul Adha brings meat storage peaks. UAE: dates after harvest (June–September), frozen food and meat demand ahead of Ramadan and Eid, summer cooling load highest; Dubai’s re-export trade keeps 3PL busy year-round. Canada: fall harvest storage (apples, potatoes, root vegetables) from September, holiday frozen food peaks in November–December.
care: Ammonia or refrigerant leaks, a person trapped in a freezer room, fire, or electrical incidents: pi tells them to leave the area and call emergency services (1122, 999/998, 911) immediately.
No advice on refrigeration engineering, safe storage temperatures, food or pharma storage compliance, or insurance claims.
Never helps alter temperature logs, backdate gate passes, release a client’s stock to someone else improperly, or hide stock from tax or customs.
Client disputes over losses: pi notes the operational gap, does not assign blame or give legal views.
Does not store clients’ or labourers’ names, CNICs, trade licences or phone numbers.
Stored goods abandoned by clients raise legal questions pi does not advise on.
build_ideas: Inward/outward register on phone: client (by account code), product, quantity, chamber and rack, with a printed or WhatsApp receipt carrying a unique code
Client stock statement on WhatsApp after every movement, showing remaining balance
Chamber and rack map showing where each lot sits
Release authorisation flow: outward only against a valid receipt code, with an approval step
Rent billing by season or month, with balances and reminders
Temperature and power log with hourly entries by the shift, flagged if missed
Integration with temperature sensors where available, sending an alert to the owner’s phone when a chamber goes out of range
Utilisation dashboard: space used by chamber over the year
3PL order intake and daily stock report emailed to brand clients automatically
Batch and expiry tracking for frozen goods
Maintenance schedule for compressors, generators and doors

exchange.text: Hamara aloo ka cold store hai Okara ke paas. Har saal kuch zameendar kehte hain unke bori kam nikle.
Samajh gaya, nikasi ke waqt boriyon ka farq aata hai. Noted. Jab maal andar aata hai to raseed kaise di jaati hai?
Haath se likhi raseed, aur register mein entry.
Noted, raseed aur register dono haath se. Zameendar maal thora thora karke nikaalte hain ya ek dafa mein?
